newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian federation minister resigns - agency.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian federation minister resigns - agency.

text.p: The Croat defence minister of Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation resigned on Monday in a letter tied to U.S. pressure for the removal of his Moslem deputy, diplomats said.
Several Western embassies received copies of the resignation letter submitted by Vladimir Soljic to federation president Kresimir Zubak.
The letter, shown to Reuters, mentioned ongoing American pressure for deputy minister Hasan Cengic's resignation.
It said speculation that Soljic's resignation would be tied to Cengic stepping down had made the defense minister's continued presence in office untenable.
The United States has refused to unload $100 million worth of military equipment bound for the federation army unless and until Cengic is removed from office because of his alleged ties with Iran.

Moslem federation officials have agreed to dump Cengic if Soljic goes as well. The papers necessary to remove the two men, signed by Moslem authorities, are sitting on Zubak's desk, awaiting his action.
Zubak, a Croat, reportedly has linked his signature to further concessions from Moslems on government reforms having nothing to do with the Defense Ministry or the U.S. arms shipment.
Federation Vice-President Ejup Ganic, a Moslem, said he had no first-hand knowledge of Soljic's resignation but said he welcomed the news.
"It could make this whole process a little easier, a little quicker," he said by telephone.
